x: SPENCER PARK--- Mick Marshall scored a useful double when he took the School 100yds and long-jump titles with 10.7 and 18'-0" respectively. He also took the short sprint in the Wandsworth District Championships.
Mick Marshall clocked 11.5 in his heat of the 100 metres and Pat Breslin and Eddie McNally recorded 3:11 and 3:20 in the 1,000 metres s'chase.

…Martin Bloice and Bill Curtin were below their bests, particularly Bill who was last in his heat and seemed very jaded. Mick Marshall produced a very useful long jump but found that another 5" was necessary to make the first six in the Youth event.…
Second places also went to Mick Marshall (Inter 100), Alan Mills (Inter High Jump) and Richard Langley (Senior 800) all failing to win by the narrowest of margins.

Mick Marshall, still a youth, recorded 3 very useful second places in the sprints and triple jump and also did a storming anchor leg in the relay.
Mick Marshall won his Club Honours Badge by achieving an A.A.A. Grade 1 Standard in the triple jump in winning the National Association Of Boys' Clubs Championship on July 25.
Shields Cup in the youths' section was Mick Marshall, with 96 points, ahead of L.

Peter Carton was our other winner at this meeting, taking the senior 800m. in 1m. 55.7s., while Mick Marshall scorched his way up the 100m. track, for second place in the senior race in 11.0s., the same time at the winner's.
He will have fine backing from LEE SULLIVAN, MICK MARSHALL, CLIFF BROOKS and CHARLIE GILLETT. 400m One of the weak spots, although I hope I'am proved wrong.
Mick Marshall, Philip Gee, Chris Martin and Lee Sullivan were third in the sprint relay, and it was particularly good to see Chris sporting a Belgrave vest again.

But the star of the meeting was junior member Mick Marshall, who took second place in the 100m. in 11.3s., second in the 200m. in 23.7s., second in the long-jump with a clearance of 20' 10", and second in the triple-jump with 39' 5".

John Martin was just under 40' in the shot-putt, while the question on everyone's lips after the long-jump was: Has Belgrave at last produced its answer to Bob Beamon? The junior match produced a more level (two-sided) contest, but a treble from Mick Marshall saw us comfortably home.

Mick Marshall, with some good sprinting, and Reg Hopkins, top of the "B" high-jumpers at 5' 8". Busiest man of the afternoon, as is often the case, was Navy man Cliff Brooks, who figured in four events, as well as the sprint relay.
In the under-18 events, the Bels came out with two winners, Mick Marshall being timed at a wind-assisted 10.9s. in the 100m., and Martin Bloice at 29.7s. in the 250m.
Martin 11.93m (39' 1¾"); 400m hurdles 3rd C. Gillett 56.8s; Junior: 100m 2nd M.
But Mick Marshall, John Martin and Reg Hopkins, Jr., were all winners in the "B" string events, and in tying for second place, with Luton, behind the Police, we were not disgraced.

One of our Spencer Park products, Mick Marshall scored a nippy win in the 200m., while in the Boys' events there was to be noticed a 16' 3" win in the long-jump by Tom Mates, the winner of the Boys' 800m. and high jump at our championship meeting the previous Saturday.
A lot of credit, however, must go to junior Mick Marshall, for his 11.3s. third in the 100m., behind Thames Valley's Martin Reynolds and Hercules Wimbledon's John Gostelow.

Steve White won the 200m., but suffered a rare reversal at the hands of a Club-mate, when junior Mick Marshall won the 100m. Mick - already a great asset - also took the junior long-jump, while Willie Williams made a jumping double in the junior events by clearing 1.52m. to win the high jump.
Mick Marshall turned out in the 100m., 200m. and 4x100m., Steve White in the 100m., 200m., 4x100m., and 4x400m., Philip Gee in the 400m. and 4x400m., and Cliff Brooks in the 4x400m. and 4x100m.

Mick Marshall's 200 metre runs have improved no end in the last few weeks and he won his heat in grand style. He took silver medal in the 100 metre race but then found that after a 3½ hour wait in the rain for the final of the longer sprint that the snap had gone out of his running.

Mick Marshall seemed to pop up everywhere, scoring well in events in which we do not usually see him. And Arnold Bentt, well, at one time his name was being called at either end of the stadium for the High Jump and Pole Vault.
Steve White and Mick Marshall had the 100m/200m pretty well sewn up, and Charlie and Phil. Gee were first past the post in both the long sprint races.

He also equalled the Championship Best Performance along with Mick Marshall in the 100 metres. Charlie Gillett finished a metre or so down in this but turned the tables when it came to the two longer sprints.
Unfortunately our sprinters suffered a set-back when Mick Marshall, after doing well in the 100m, TJ and LJ, "pulled" a hamstring in the 'B' 200m and had to step out of the relay squad.
BELGRAVE H (P.Williamson, M.Marshall, C.Gillett, P.Gee) 45.1; 4 x 400m: 3. BELGRAVE H (A.Mead, P.Williamson, D.Wiseman, P.Gee) 3:32.2; 3000m SC: 4.
It is in the sprints, however, that we are at our most powerful, Steve White's flowing movement contrasting with Mick Marshall's power-house action but both with the same effect.

Mick Marshall narrowly beat Charlie Gillett in a tight 200m, having gained 3rd in the 100m and Philip Gee was at his most aggressive, tearing out that first 200m in the one lap event and hanging on to gain a medal.

But with only two other winners, Charlie Gillett and Mick Marshall, we were not good enough to hold the Essex Club. We can only pride ourselves on seeing how obviously pleased these clubs are when they do manage to defeat Belgrave.
